stories.headline: Sources: 49ers George Kittle, Nick Bosa make trip to Australia
stories.summary: 49ers tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa will both make Wednesday's trip to Australia to play the Rams, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.body:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa will both make Wednesday's trip to Australia to play the Los Angeles Rams, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Kittle, who was activated from the physically unable to perform list on Aug. 23, is recovering from a torn right Achilles suffered during the Jan. 11 playoff win against the Philadelphia Eagles. He will make the trip after two positive days of practice and is trending in the right direction to play in the season opener, per sources.

In the days after the injury, Kittle insisted he wouldn't miss much of the 2026 season, if any, in part because the tear happened higher up in his leg, which promotes better blood flow and recovery.

Bosa, who tore his ACL last September, did not practice for most of training camp, but is ramping up with his knee. It was his third ACL surgery and second on his right knee.

The 49ers open the season against the Rams on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia.

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA analysis, rankings, rosters
stories.summary: Sixteen nations will compete in the World Cup in Berlin starting Friday. Team USA and France are front-runners.
stories.body:
The WNBA season is paused for the next couple of weeks, but there's plenty of women's basketball being played. The 2026 FIBA World Cup begins Friday and will run through Sept. 13 in Berlin, Germany. The tournament might not be as prominent as the Olympics -- to fans, at least -- but it is one of two major international competitions, with this year's event featuring 16 teams from North America, Europe, Asia and Africa.

The United States is, per usual, stacked, though the reigning champions suffered a blow when it was announced Monday that four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum are unable to participate in the tournament due to health reasons. But those losses don't alter the task at hand: bringing home a fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall.

The U.S. women's national team plays its group phase opener Friday against China. The USA faces Italy on Sunday and then Czechia on Monday. If the U.S. women win their group, they move on to the quarterfinals on Sept. 10, with the semifinals set for Sept. 12 and the championship and third-place games on Sept. 13.

There are plenty of other familiar faces in Berlin, too, with dozens of current and former WNBA players representing other countries, from Australia to Türkiye.

ESPN's World Cup guide gets you set with everything you need to know before the games tip. Not every roster has been finalized yet, but we list current WNBA players on each squad, along with their stats for this current WNBA season.

Jump to:

AUS | BEL | CHN | CZE | FRA | GER

HUN | ITA | JPN | KOR | MLI | NGR

PUR | ESP | TUR | USA | GROUPS

1. United States
Current WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever (16.9 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 1.3 BPG)

G Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings (20.5 PPG, 5.9 APG, 4.1 RPG)

G Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics (16.8 PPG, 4.3 APG, 1.2 SPG)

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever (22.5 PPG, 8.4 APG, 3.9 RPG)

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx (18.0 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 1.4 SPG)

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury (21.3 PPG, 3.6 RPG, 1.9 APG)

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces (12.0 PPG, 6.8 APG, 1.4 SPG)

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream (18.3 PPG, 3.6 APG, 2.3 SPG)

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics (15.3 PPG, 9.4 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream (16.1 PPG, 12.4 RPG, 1.8 SPG)

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty (20.4 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.4 BPG)

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces (18.9 PPG, 6.6 APG, 4.4 RPG)

Outlook: The U.S. women's national basketball team is home to one of the most dominant dynasties in all of sports, winning eight consecutive Olympic gold medals and four straight World Cups. The program has lost just one game at a major international competition since 1994 -- the semifinals of the 2006 World Championship (later renamed World Cup) against Russia, where the Americans won bronze. Team USA has since won 30 consecutive World Cup games.

That is the legacy newly minted national team director Sue Bird, senior national team coach Kara Lawson and this young U.S. squad -- a group with seven players under 27 -- bring to Berlin. Fans have long anticipated seeing the likes of Clark, Bueckers and Reese compete against international competition as part of the senior national team. They got a taste of that at the World Cup qualifying tournament, where the USA went 5-0 and won by an average margin of 42 points.

But between the grueling schedule, heighted competition and pressure of representing the USA, the World Cup will be a much greater challenge. USA Basketball's youth movement will be tested even more so with Wilson, the reigning World Cup and Olympics MVP, and Plum no longer available. But they still have a core of experienced veterans in Stewart, Gray, Collier, Young and Copper, who know what it takes to win gold. -- Alexa Philippou

2. France
Current WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty (9.2 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 3.4 APG)

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury (6.3 PPG, 2.7 RPG, 1.3 APG)

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty (8.5 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 2.4 APG)

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun (11.6 PPG, 1.9 RPG, 4.6 APG)

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire (15.9 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 6.3 APG)

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm (17.0 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 BPG)

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries (12.9 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.2 APG)

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries (14.3 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 2.2 APG)

Other notable players: C Marieme Badiane

Outlook: France, seen as the top threat to Team USA, might have its most talented roster ever with eight active WNBA players, four of whom will be headed to the playoffs. France has been building as an international power for the last several years. The French nearly toppled Team USA in the Olympic final in Paris in 2024, falling 67-66 behind former UConn star Williams' 19 points. France also took Olympic silver in 2012 and bronze in 2021.

France's only medal in the World Cup was a bronze in 1953, the first year of the event, but they are expected to have a podium finish this year. Malonga, the 2025 No. 2 WNBA draft pick who dunked in the All-Star Game in July, might look to do that in the World Cup. -- Michael Voepel

3. Spain

Current WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty (1.4 PPG, 1.1 RPG, 0.3 APG)

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo (8.9 PPG, 4.6 RPG, 2.6 APG)

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire (13.2 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 0.6 BPG)

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm (10.3 PPG, 5.7 RPG, 0.9 SPG)

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics (3.3 PPG, 2.0 APG, 0.6 SPG)

Other notable players: G Iyana Martin, G Maite Cazorla

Outlook: Spain has had a relatively quiet output on the international stage in recent years. They medaled at the World Cup in 2010, 2014 and 2018 and took silver at the 2016 Olympics -- but then didn't even qualify for the previous World Cup in 2022 or the podium in Paris.

Coming off a silver-medal finish at last year's EuroBasket -- and more recently giving the USA its closest game of March's qualifying tournament -- Spain could be poised for a big showing in Berlin. The team is led by veteran Alba Torrens, the only player with World Cup experience, and has a naturalized star in DiLeo, who was a top-five scorer at the 2024 Olympics. Carrera has seen limited time with the Liberty but has been much more productive with her national team. What might be most anticipated, though, is the emergence of Spain's young tandem of 20-year-old stars in Storm rookie Fam and Martin, the Fire's draft-and-stash first-round selection. -- Philippou

4. Belgium

Current WNBA players:

G Julie Allemand, Toronto Tempo (6.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 5.6 APG)

C Kyara Linskens, Phoenix Mercury (3.0 PPG, 2.4 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

F Antonia Delaere, Minnesota Lynx (2.9 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 1.1 APG)

Other notable players: F Emma Meesseman, G Julie Vanloo, F Bethy Mununga

Outlook: Belgium should be one of the powers of Group C, along with Australia. The Cats are coached by longtime former WNBA coach Mike Thibault, who won a title with the Washington Mystics in 2019 when Meesseman was WNBA Finals MVP. Meesseman has played nine seasons in the WNBA, most recently last year when she spent 20 games (including the playoffs) with the New York Liberty. Vanloo played briefly (five games) with the Liberty this season. This is Allemand's fourth season in the WNBA, and she has been a starter for the expansion Tempo. This is Belgium's third World Cup appearance; they finished fourth in 2018 and fifth in 2022. Belgium has not medaled at the Olympics but had its best finish in Paris in 2024, falling in the bronze medal game. -- Voepel

5. Germany

Projected WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire (6.3 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 0.7 APG)

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty (10.2 PPG, 3.0 RPG, 1.1 SPG)

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire (4.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.3 APG)

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo (12.3 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 0.9 BPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Just like in the Olympics, a World Cup host faces a mixture of pressure and opportunity, and it's no different for Germany in what is just its second time participating in the event (and first since 1998). Unfortunately the Germans will be without the services of star Satou Sabally, who has stepped away from basketball while recovering from the effects of her second concussion in eight months, and it's unclear how healthy her sister, Nyara, will be. For the Germans to earn their first podium finish at a major international competition, they will need a huge tournament from Fiebich, who has been showcasing her value with the Liberty upon returning from injury. But also expect the likes of Buhner and Geiselsoder to play even bigger roles than they do stateside in Portland. Germany is coached by Olaf Lange, current Tempo associate head coach and Sandy Brondello's husband. -- Philippou

6. China

Projected WNBA players:

C Han Xu, New York Liberty (6.4 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

C Li Yueru, Dallas Wings (3.3 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 0.3 BPG)

* Roster is not yet finalized

Outlook: China should be the toughest challenger to Team USA in Group D, and the two play in the event opener for both. The United States and China faced off twice at the 2022 World Cup, with the U.S. women winning by 14 in group play and by 22 in the gold medal match. That result was still a win for the Chinese, though, as it marked the first time since 1994 that they earned a medal at a major international competition (both were silvers).

China faltered at the 2024 Olympics, finishing in ninth, before punching its ticket to the World Cup at this spring's qualifying tournament in Wuhan. This roster has some new faces compared to that '22 squad, headlined by the 7-foot-2, 19-year-old Zhang Ziyu. But she's not the only player who could pose some trouble for the USA, as the more experienced Han Xu (6-11) and Li Yueru (6-7) bring additional height, with FIBA dubbing the trio the "Triple Towers." -- Philippou

7. Australia

Current WNBA players:

F Chloe Bibby, Minnesota Lynx (2.3 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

G Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream (4.6 PPG, 1.5 RPG, 1.0 APG)

C Ezi Magbegor, Seattle Storm (6.9 PPG, 4.0 RPG, 1.2 BPG)

G Jade Melbourne, Seattle Storm (9.5 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 3.9 APG)

F Alanna Smith, Dallas Wings (6.0 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.0 APG)

G Miela Sowah, Golden State Valkyries (0.3 PPG, 0.8 RPG)

F Stephanie Talbot, Las Vegas Aces (3.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.0 APG)

Other notable players: F Alex Fowler, G Alex Wilson

Outlook: Phoenix Mercury guard Sami Whitcomb, captain of the Australian team, had to withdraw from the World Cup last week because of an ongoing knee injury. It's a big blow to the Opals regarding leadership and scoring. And it's heartbreaking for Whitcomb, who is 38. She was replaced by Sowah, 26. Sandy Brondello, who won WNBA titles with the Mercury (2014) and New York Liberty (2024) and is now with the Toronto Tempo, is Australia's coach.

The Opals began to emerge as an international power in women's basketball in the 1980s and won their first World Cup medal with a bronze in 1998. Their highlight was 2006, when they defeated Russia for the gold medal after the Russians had upset the United States in the semifinals. They also won bronze in 2002, 2014 and 2022, and took silver in 2018. Australia's six total World Cup medals puts them third on the all-time medal chart. The Aussies also have six Olympic medals: three silvers and three bronzes. -- Voepel

8. Italy

Current WNBA players:

G Costanza Verona, Dallas Wings (developmental player)

F Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries (8.8 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 1.8 APG)

Other notable players: F Lorela Cubaj

Outlook: Italy is enjoying a resurgence on the FIBA stage: Last year the team won its first EuroBasket medal since 1995 by beating France for the bronze medal, and now this World Cup marks the country's first appearance at a major international competition since the 1996 Olympics. Led by Zandalasini, the Italians lost 93-59 to the United States at the qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico, but went 4-1 overall at the event, including upsetting Spain the day after playing the U.S. women (and it's largely the same squad Italy has in Berlin). Italy has a difficult path ahead, though, having to face both the USA and China, the 2022 World Cup silver medalist, in the group phase. -- Philippou

9. Nigeria

Projected WNBA players:

F Amy Okonkwo, Portland Fire (4.3 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.3 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: This is the fourth time Nigeria has qualified for the World Cup, although it withdrew in 2022. That was much to the chagrin of the Nigerian players and FIBA. It was a decision by the Nigerian government, which opted in May 2022 to withdraw all its basketball teams from international competition while it restructured the sport's governance. Nigeria earned its World Cup berth this time by winning the AfroBasket 2025 championship. The team still played in the World Cup qualifying tournament in France in March, but lost three of five games. Nigeria's best finish in the World Cup is eighth, in 2018. The team's best Olympic finish is also eighth, in 2024. -- Voepel

10. Japan

Current WNBA players:

G Mai Yamamoto, Las Vegas Aces (5.8 PPG, 1.8 APG, 0.8 SPG)

Other notable players: G Rui Machida, G Kokoro Tanaka, C Ramu Tokashiki

Outlook: American basketball fans have come to enjoy Japan's entertaining style of play in recent years, particularly since squaring off against the USA in the 2020 Olympic gold medal game. Japan is known for speed, movement and 3-point shooting, which means the team can beat anyone if it gets hot -- and can lose to anyone if it can't hit shots. Lack of size is often an Achilles' heel -- just one player, Tokashiki, is listed over 6-foot.

Still, look out for the likes of Yamamoto, a midseason addition to the Aces, as well as Golden State draft pick Tanaka to make a splash on the perimeter. After the high of clinching silver at the Tokyo Olympics, Japan finished ninth at the 2022 World Cup, 12th at the Paris Olympics and almost didn't qualify for Berlin. Corey Gaines, the coach of the 2009 Phoenix Mercury championship squad, took over as head coach in early 2025. The pressure is on for them to find their form going into 2030, when they will host the next World Cup. -- Philippou

11. Hungary

Projected WNBA players:

F Dorka Juhász, Minnesota Lynx (3.8 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.2 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: While France is a big favorite in Group B, Hungary might make some waves behind Juhász. That especially could be the case with JiSu Park out for Korea and Nigeria looking kind of inconsistent entering the tournament. Hungary is making its sixth appearance in the World Cup but first since 1998. The team's best finish was fifth in 1957. -- Voepel

12. Korea

Current WNBA players:

G Jihyun Park, Los Angeles Sparks (2.2 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.5 APG)

Outlook: Korea is typically known as a strong outside shooting team. The team will need to rely even more on its guards with center JiSu Park, who played three seasons with the Las Vegas Aces, out due to an ankle injury. Korea is making its 18th World Cup appearance; it has played in every tournament except the first two in 1953 and 1957. Korea has won two silver medals, in 1967 and 1979. The team also has finished fourth three times, most recently in 2002. Korea has one medal in Olympic play, a silver in 1984. -- Voepel

13. Türkiye

Projected WNBA players:

G/F Kennedy Burke, Connecticut Sun (8.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 1.4 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Türkiye will learn a lot about its chances from its opener vs. Belgium. This is Türkiye's third appearance in the World Cup; the team was fourth in 2014, when it hosted the event, and 10th in 2018. In her seventh year in the WNBA, Burke is having a career-best season. -- Voepel

14. Mali

Projected WNBA players:

G Aicha Coulibaly, Chicago Sky (4.8 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Sika Kone, Atlanta Dream (1.7 PPG, 1.0 RPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Mali will make its third World Cup appearance, where it hopes to improve on an 11th-place finish in 2022. The program established itself as the second-best team out of Africa behind Nigeria, which beat Mali in the 2025 AfroBasket final. But Mali followed that up with a promising showing during the qualifying tournament in March, beating Czechia and narrowly losing to Brazil to clinch a spot in Berlin. Maimouna Haidara was the team's leading scorer in Wuhan, followed by the Dream's Kone; they'll need those two to dazzle to cause some upsets in Group A. -- Philippou

15. Czechia

Current WNBA players:

G Eliska Joklova, Minnesota Lynx (1.7 PPG, 1.1 APG, 1.0 RPG)

Outlook: Czechia is back at the World Cup after last appearing in the event in 2014; in 2010, it was the host nation and earned silver. The team's return this year has already been met with some concern. Czechia eked into the World Cup after a tepid qualifying tournament and has had some bad injury luck to two key players: Emma Cechova tore her ACL three games into her season with the Minnesota Lynx after a promising start, while Julia Reisingerova is also unavailable due to injury. On top of that, Czechia has to face the United States, China and a surging Italy squad in group play. It'll need sensational outings from the likes of Lynx rookie Joklova (née Hamzova), Veronika Vorackova and Petra Holesinska to keep up. -- Philippou

16. Puerto Rico

Current WNBA players: None

Other notable players: G Arella Guirantes, C Imani McGee-Stafford

Outlook: Host Puerto Rico was fourth in the qualifying tournament won by the United States in March in San Juan. A tough group awaits in Berlin, especially having to face Australia and Belgium. This is Puerto Rico's third appearance in the World Cup, having finished 16th in 2018 and eighth in 2022. Guirantes played two seasons in the WNBA, most recently in 2023. McGee-Stafford played four seasons in the league, most recently in 2019. Puerto Rico has competed twice in the Olympics. -- Voepel

Groups

Sixteen teams will compete in the FIBA World Cup in Berlin, Germany, with 36 games being played over 10 days from Sept. 4 to Sept. 13. The first-place team in each group advances to the quarterfinals; the second- and third-place teams will qualify for a single-game elimination format to determine the rest of the quarterfinalists.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. stories.headline: U.S. MLS teams to make full return to Open Cup in 2027
stories.summary: All 27 United States-based MLS teams will compete in the 2027 edition of the U.S. Open Cup for the first time since 2023.
stories.body:
All 27 United States-based MLS teams will compete in the 2027 U.S. Open Cup, marking the tournament's first year with full league participation since 2023.

MLS has lifted the rule capping clubs at two non-league competitions, allowing qualified teams to feature in the U.S Open Cup, Leagues Cup and Concacaf Champions Cup in addition to the regular season.

Only 16 United States-based MLS clubs participated in the 2026 edition of the U.S. Open Cup, while 18 MLS clubs, including those based in Canada, participated in the Leagues Cup.

Clubs will enter the tournament in the round of 64 beginning in July of next year to align with the start of the new summer-to-spring MLS competition schedule for the 2027-28 regular season.

MLS clubs will also receive hosting priority for their opening match of the competition.

"The Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup connects all leagues, clubs and fans in a unique way," said Nelson Rodriguez, MLS executive vice president of sporting and matchday. "For MLS clubs, it's a chance to write a special chapter in the tournament's history and earn qualification to the Concacaf Champions Cup."

A live draw will then be held after the round of 64 to determine the round-of-32 and round-of-16 matches and hosting privileges.

The 2027 U.S. Open Cup round of 32 is set to be played on Sept.14 and Sept. 15, while round-of-16 dates will be confirmed at a later time. The competition will then resume for the quarterfinals on Nov. 23-24, with the semifinals on Dec. 1 and the final on Dec. 15.

The tournament will also amend certain roster rules for the upcoming edition, expanding gameday squads from 18 players to 20.

"MLS clubs may select from any contracted first-team, MLS NEXT Pro, and academy players. This flexibility helps provide younger players with competitive minutes while allowing clubs to manage multiple competitions," MLS said in a news release.

The 2026 edition of the U.S. Open Cup remains ongoing, with four MLS teams competing in the semifinals, set for Sept. 16.

The 2002 Open Cup champion Columbus Crew will host 2022 champion Orlando City SC in the first semifinal, while the Colorado Rapids host St. Louis City in the second.

The winner of the Columbus-Orlando contest will host the final on Oct. 21.

stories.headline: Police talk to four Sydney men in AFL sex assault probe
stories.summary: Four Sydney men have been interviewed by police weeks after three women reported alleged sexual assaults during a hotel room party after an AFL match.
stories.body:
Four Sydney men have been interviewed by police weeks after three women reported alleged sexual assaults during a hotel room party after an AFL match.

Sydney Swans players Chad Warner, Isaac Heeney, Riley Bice, Nick Blakey and James Jordon were reportedly partying with adult entertainers in a room at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne on August 17 when the alleged assaults took place.

Three women made a report to Victoria Police.

Detectives confirmed they travelled to NSW this week to interview four men, including a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Paddington man and two Randwick men aged 25 and 26.

Three other men who police believe were in the room at the time were interviewed solely as witnesses.

Police are not looking to speak with anyone else in relation to the investigation.

No charges have been laid and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing.

An update to the investigation was not expected for at least eight weeks, police said.

The Swans have "categorically" stated none of their staff were in the hotel room and are not involved in the investigation.

The club is refusing to comment about the investigation or the on-field future of the five players, who remain exiled from the club as they serve season-long suspensions for a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

"The wellbeing of those impacted remains of paramount importance," a Swans spokesperson said on Wednesday in a statement acknowledging the latest police update.

"We note that no charges have been laid and that police have indicated the process may take some time to run its course."

Swans coach Dean Cox has vowed to always "support my players".

"I'm staying in dialogue with those five players whilst they're away from the football club," Cox told Fox Footy on Tuesday night.

"I speak about their welfare, how they're going and if we can support in any way.

"I haven't spoken to them at all about the police investigation."

The AFL's integrity unit is investigating.

"Once the police investigation is complete, we will conduct our own enquiries, but the AFL won't get involved while there's a police investigation under way," AFL chief executive Andrew Dillon said last week.

Two legal firms have been engaged by the women to probe potential civil claims.

stories.body:
Formula 1 action is back in full swing and next up on the calendar is Monza, also known as the "Temple of Speed."

McLaren's Lando Norris sealed back-to-back victories after winning the Dutch Grand Prix to kick off the second half of the season last time out.

Kimi Antonelli is leading the championship by 59 points and following behind is his teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both in second.

The Italian youngster will be hit with a grid penalty at his home race for taking a new engine.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know about the Italian Grand Prix.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Franco Colapinto signs new contract to stay at Alpine for 2027

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Italian Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza

The "Temple of Speed" is known for it's long straights and heavy braking zones, and is the fastest track in Formula 1 history by overall average lap speed.

It's another classic circuit that has been on the calendar since 1950, only missing one year of racing in 1980 due to upgrading the track infrastructure.

It has one of the best podiums in the world as the famous Ferrari-loving tifosi flood onto the track after the race is finished. It's always a sight to be seen, especially if you are a Ferrari driver or an Italian driver.

Italian Grand Prix

Circuit: Autodromo Nazionale Monza; Monza, Italy

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg, Mercedes

2017: Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes

2018: Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes

2019: Charles Leclerc, Ferrari

2020: Pierre Gasly, AlphaTauri

2021: Daniel Ricciardo, McLaren

2022: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

2023: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

2024: Charles Leclerc, Ferrari

2025: Max Verstappen, Red Bull

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1950

Lap record: 1:18.792, Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Laps: 53 laps of 5.8km. Total distance 306km

Most poles: Lewis Hamilton has seven at this circuit (2009, 2012, 2014-2017, 2020). Other pole sitters from the grid are Fernando Alonso (2007, 2010), Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022), Max Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton (2012, 2014-2015, 2017-2018) and Michael Schumacher (1996, 1998, 2000, 2003, 2006) are tied on five wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Fernando Alonso (2007, 2010), Pierre Gasly (2020), Charles Leclerc (2019, 2024) and Max Verstappen (2022, 2023 and 2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Italian Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny all weekend with light winds, with highs of 32°C on Sunday.

What happened last year?

Max Verstappen set the pace with the fastest lap in F1 history after getting pole position in Monza.

The Dutchman set a time of 1:18.792 breaking Hamilton's record from 2020.

It was McLaren's Norris who was on provisional pole before Verstappen beat him to the line in the closing stages.

Verstappen then went on to win the race in commanding fashion, but there were some team orders taking place at McLaren.

Norris was running in second for the majority of the race, but after a slow pit-stop, the team asked Oscar Piastri to move aside and let him teammate back through for second place.

At the time, Piastri was leading the championship from Norris by 31 points.

Who will win this year?

The biggest news entering the weekend will be Antonelli's engine penalty that will hamper his opportunity to score maximum points during the race.

He leads the championship after winning six races, but title fights can change quickly, as we saw during the backend of the 2025 season.

McLaren's upgrades have certainly been working, but team boss Andrea Stella said that Monza will be the true benchmark in terms of its performance and progress.

Ferrari will be hungry to get a home win with either of its drivers, but Monza will typically suit those strong in straight line speed and high-speed corners, such as Mercedes.

Monza could be one of the best opportunities to close the gap in the title race and take advantage of Antonelli not being a threat at the front of the pack.

stories.headline: Which fantasy hockey league is right for you?
stories.summary: Roto vs H2H points? Dynasty vs redraft? With all the scoring settings, roster setup and more, here's your first stop when signing up for an ESPN Fantasy Hockey league.
stories.body:
So you've decided to take the fantasy hockey plunge, joining millions of others in enjoying one of the sporting world's best game within a game. Welcome. Or perhaps you've already waded through these puck-friendly fantasy waters and feel inspired to dive into a different type of pool. Preseason greetings to you too. Either way, leaving other customizable options (roster size, lineup rules, bench flexibility, IR spots etc.) alone for now, here's a rundown of ESPN Fantasy's variety of fantasy hockey leagues, available to suit any taste.

H2H Points

The most popular game in ESPN's fantasy hockey universe pits individual managers against others in weekly head-to-head fisticuffs with a slew of weighted points at stake. Most total points wins the week 1-0 - no fuss, no muss. While always customizable to your own statistical taste, our default 12-category game presents as follows:

Goals (G) 2
Assists (A) 1
Power Play Points (PPP) .5
Short Handed Points (SHP) .5
Shots on Goal ( SOG) .1
Hits (HIT) .1
Blocked Shots (BLK) .5
Goaltender Wins (W) 4
Goals Against (GA) -2
Saves (SV) .2
Shutouts (SO) 3
Overtime Losses (OTL) 1

In stride with this formula, skaters who shoot regularly, score plentifully, and contribute often on the power play, qualify as fantasy royalty. But those characters are limited in number. Once the elite are spoken for, especially on larger fantasy rosters, there's much to appreciate about prolific shot-blockers who also chip in on offense on occasion. Think defenseman Jacob Trouba. An evening's haul including an assist, three hits, four shots, and three blocked, and -- without much obvious fantasy fanfare -- he's racked up 3.1 fantasy points. An above-average haul by any fantasy measure.

Furthermore, not unlike in the living, breathing game itself, goaltending matters. There are too many fantasy points at stake to pooh-pooh the position. While having good goaltending won't ensure a triumphant turn by April, rolling out sub-mediocre players on weak teams most certainly guarantees the opposite. Doesn't matter who you have up front. Pay the role proper mind, or pay a sad fantasy price.

In considering any player, spending a few moments in assessing the individual, by doing a little bit of simple arithmetic -- what is their potential fantasy sum? -- is the most sure-fire way to earn rich fantasy dividends in H2H points leagues. Whether it's during the draft or in evaluating free agent/trade commodities through the season.

H2H Categories

Varying from the H2H points formula, so-called "each" category leagues also maintain a committed, loyal following. Managers engaged in this style of contest, where stat egalitarianism reigns, are best served by striving for competitive balance. Each category, in direct head-to-head competition, is equal to each other in that goals, hits, blocked shots, whatever-your-fantasy-fancy etc. counts towards the week's final score, accruing over the course of the season. You've earned 31 shots on goal and your opponent has 30? You win that category, full stop.

Again, margin of victory in individual categories, large or small, matters not. Beating your competitor in hits by a singular check carries equal weight to obliterating them in goals. Since defeating your direct rival 10-2 in a 12 category format is a significantly bigger victory than edging them 6-5-1, you want to give yourself a competitive chance in all/most aspects of the fantasy game. Top-tier, well-rounded players are extra valuable in battling for a favorable blowout, especially on small rosters. For example, Florida's Brady Tkachuk checks a bunch of valuable boxes, night in and night out, in fantasy leagues that reward both scoring and physical play. Loading up on specialists in one category is much less useful than in other forms of H2H play. A balanced smorgasbord of skilled contributors in all aspects of the game will provide you with the greatest chance of campaign-long success.

H2H Most Categories

This type of league operates in similar fashion to "each" category competition except whichever manager emerges with the weekly victory wins 1-0. You win the week or you lose it, regardless of final tally. A 6-5-1 win is just as good as 12-0. In this case, the strategy of loading up on players who satisfy most stats, as opposed to striving for balance across the fantasy board, has merit. If you're rocking out in eight or nine of 12 categories, maybe don't sweat penalty minutes, or time-on-ice or the like too much. Securing a few "slam-dunk" categories at the expense of one or two others makes greater sense in this particular brand of fantasy play. Please don't draft a singular skater with an impressive plus/minus at the expense of nailing down shots on net. You're only increasing your odds of losing both categories.

It also bears repeating: Goaltenders cannot be shrugged off in any brand of H2H league, including this type, when more than two categories are devoted to the position. Please don't try to convince yourself otherwise.

Rotisserie (Roto)

Interested in a slow-burn, largely unforgiving league that can't be won in the first few months of the season but certainly can be lost? Willing to accept the challenge of assembling a roster with little margin for weakness, similar to how it's done IRL? Then this brand of fantasy play might be for you. As with H2H Categories competition, constructing and maintaining a balanced fantasy squad is vital in Roto leagues. Only more so. In direct competition with every other manager at all times, striving for a share of points available based on standings in individual categories, squandering one or two can prove catastrophically costly.

Sitting top spot in goals or ATOI or hits etc. in a 12-team/10-category league translates into 12 of a possible 12 points. Sitting dead last converts into a single point. That's a massive gap. Which is why ranking worst or near-bottom in a couple of stats, and subsequently earning only a point or two of a maximum of 12, is difficult to overcome, regardless of how well you're faring otherwise. By no means a gateway league, Roto competition best suits managers with strong fantasy stomachs. But that also means victory, when achieved, tastes all the sweeter after such a season-long grind.

Season Points

The ESPN Fantasy version that most closely resembles the lesser-nuanced game of your elders, where everyone gathered at the pub for an evening, armed with a pen, paper, and magazine, and selected their players for the year. Teams accrued points based on scoring and goaltending, and whichever side finished with the highest total, won.

Of course, there are many ways to cyber-customize your points league with other categories, trades, free-agent acquisitions, roster limits, and varying lineup adjustment windows. Daily or weekly, it's up to you. But the founding philosophy remains the same: the best overall team by season's end sports the crown. While this style of league lacks the charm of despising another individual manager over seven exclusive days in head-to-head combat, it -- unlike classic roto leagues -- serves as an excellent introduction for newbie managers to get their feet wet. Especially those who don't want to devote as much time, at least to start.

Dynasty/Keeper vs. Single Season

There are advantages to both. While dynasty/keeper competition is more kindred to how real teams are run -- management doesn't get to start from scratch every year in the NHL -- with redraft leagues, there's the benefit of enjoying a clean slate the following season, no matter how badly a current campaign is unfolding. But there's inarguably a greater sense of satisfaction with enjoying fantasy success on the blades of a roster built over time, from rebuild to peak performance. In stricter dynasty leagues, where few bodies move in or out, it's often nifty to maintain relationships with players from their rookie debuts, well into the veteran years. For many then, keeper competition -- middle ground between an all-in dynasty and turn-the-page redraft play -- will suit you best. Selecting six to eight keepers every campaign is a common tact, still allowing for improvement from outside help at season's onset. No one's going to relinquish Connor McDavid as a keeper, but some very good players will inevitably re-enter the draft in these modified leagues.

Again, there's no right or wrong way to play ESPN Fantasy Hockey. Depending on how much time and energy you want to invest - from the bare minimum to managing your squad as a quasi part-time job - it's all about customizing whichever league feels most up your own fantasy alley. And enjoying this great game through a fun bonus lens from late summer until it all wraps up in the spring.

Ready to play? Sign up for free today!

stories.headline: EFL criticises UEFA after rescheduling three domestic fixtures
stories.summary: The English Football League has accused UEFA of an "unwillingness to cooperate" after it says the European governing body's stance forced them to rearrange three domestic fixtures.
stories.body:
The English Football League has accused UEFA of an "unwillingness to cooperate" after it says the European governing body's stance forced them to rearrange three domestic fixtures.

Everton and Wolves were scheduled to play their Carabao Cup third-round tie on Sept. 9 before Liverpool and Atlético Madrid's Champions League clash was, on Saturday, announced for the same day.

As a result, that contest and two others -- Liverpool and Tottenham in the League Cup and Wolves vs. Portsmouth in the Championship -- have been rescheduled.

An EFL statement read: "On Saturday, UEFA announced that it had scheduled Liverpool v Atlético Madrid for the same date, despite it being clear that Everton and Liverpool cannot play home fixtures on the same evening.

"The EFL met with UEFA officials on Monday morning to explore available options, however in those discussions it was made clear that they were unwilling to consider rescheduling the Liverpool v Atlético Madrid fixture due to the impact on supporters travelling from overseas.

"Disappointingly, the League has therefore been forced to make changes.

"Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA Club competitions -- a decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues.

"These changes have included splitting Carabao Cup round three ties across two weeks, and implementing draw conditions for round three which prevent scheduling conflicts for clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

- Champions League draw becomes UEFA's latest stand against FIFA president Infantino

- Champions League draw: Good games for Liverpool, bad for Barcelona

"This makes UEFA's unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five impacted clubs, and we sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused."

UEFA, in response, insisted it "always does its best to accommodate reasonable requests", but said the "potential conflict" only emerged after fixtures were published, when changes were no longer possible.

The European governing body said in a statement: "UEFA regularly receives scheduling requests from associations, leagues and clubs and always does its best to accommodate reasonable requests wherever possible.

"In this case, no issue had been raised with UEFA during the scheduling process, and the potential conflict only became apparent after the publication of the fixture lists.

"At that stage, it was not possible to make changes, particularly given the significant number of supporters who may already have arranged international travel and accommodation. We believe that these commitments deserve to be respected.

"UEFA remains in contact with the relevant stakeholders, and we appreciate all efforts to minimise any local operational challenges."

Everton vs. Wolves is now set for Wednesday, Sept. 16; Liverpool vs. Tottenham, originally slated for Sept. 16, is now a day earlier and Wolves vs. Portsmouth, also initially due to be played on Sept. 16, will take place on Oct. 20.

stories.headline: PNG's Young pursuit on hold after salary-cap drama
stories.summary: PNG will hold off pursuing Hudson Young after they were told their proposed offer for the Canberra star would not meet market value.
stories.body:
PNG will hold off pursuing Hudson Young after they were told their proposed offer for the Canberra star would not meet market value.

Just two days after Young confirmed he was attracted to the prospect of joining the Chiefs' star-studded roster, the potential move has hit a serious sticking point.

It is understood the Chiefs were looking to offer Young about $900,000 a season, if the NSW State of Origin star joined the NRL's 19th franchise for 2028.

That figure is close to $200,000 shy of the monster three-year deal worth $1.1 million a season believed to have been pitched by the Raiders to keep the back-rower.

Young had planned to tour PNG in coming weeks once off crutches following his Achilles rupture, while seriously contemplating becoming the Chiefs' eighth signing.

But ARL Commission chairman Peter V'landys told club bosses on Wednesday that PNG would definitely need to meet market value on player signings.

The NRL has several tools to measure market value, including benchmarking of the highest-paid players in each position and salaries of similar players.

The value of other offers could also be taken into account, while the NRL traditionally will allow players to be paid less than that if there are valid reasons.

Ultimately, it means the Chiefs will have to go very close to matching Canberra's mega offer.

Until Wednesday, the Chiefs had believed an offer of $900,000 would have met market value for Young.

AAP understands they were willing to up their offer to $950,000 a year, but that is also not expected to be enough.

With that in mind, Chiefs officials have decided to wait until at least November 1 to make a call on Young, when he becomes a free agent.

PNG bosses are also mindful that they have signed seven players, and need to be careful in their evaluation of potential recruits with 18 months until they actually play.

Clubs have grown concerned in recent months about the Chiefs' signing spree, given the tax-free incentives on offer for players who join the club.

Penrith coach Ivan Cleary claimed last month it was near impossible to compete with the Chiefs on the open market, if a player decided they were happy to move there.

What the NRL's move means for the rest of PNG's signings remains to be seen, and if clubs desperate for a big name are able to drastically impact the market.

Penrith star Nathan Cleary is among a host of big names off contract next year and able to talk with rivals from November 1, and he could attract deals as high as $2 million.

Speaking this week, Young had suggested he would only leave Canberra for the Chiefs in 2028.

"I have no interest in playing for another NRL club," Young said.

"Sticky (coach Ricky Stuart) and I have spoken about that. It's more the opportunity of the PNG thing.

"My mindset is pretty open. It's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. I just want to make sure I am comfortable with the decision I make."

stories.headline: Premier League sets new record for transfer spending
stories.summary: The Premier League set a new record for transfer spending as the window closed with a flurry of deals.
stories.body:
The Premier League set a new record for transfer spending as the window closed with a flurry of deals.

More than half of the top flight's clubs broke their transfer records in a summer window featuring four of the most expensive ever signings.

The final two days of the window pushed summer spending significantly beyond last season's record of £3.14 billion ($4.23bn) with confirmed figures exceeding £3.3b ($4.4bn).

First Liverpool spent an initial £106 million ($144m) potentially rising to £123m ($165m) on Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, then City paired Elliot Anderson with another nine-figure midfielder in former Chelsea star Enzo Fernández -- whose £125m ($168m) move matched the British record set 12 months ago by Barcola's new teammate Alexander Isak.

Earlier in the summer, England internationals Anderson and Morgan Rogers joined Manchester City for £116m ($156m) and Chelsea for £117m ($157m) respectively.

Sandro Tonali's move from Newcastle to Tottenham has the potential to become a fifth £100m-plus ($134.8m-plus) deal this summer, with the initial £92.5m ($124.6m) marking the second time Spurs had broken their club record as it came hot on the heels of Mateus Fernandes' £85m ($114.5m) arrival from West Ham.

Savio's £75m ($101m) switch from City slotted in third on Spurs' all-time list, with manager Roberto De Zerbi admitting "the transfer market is crazy" -- reflecting a league-wide summer of spending.

Eleven clubs in all have broken their transfer records, six of them on more than one occasion.

Coventry have done so four times over, signing Aurèle Amenda for an initial £15.4m ($20.7m) before Loum Tchaouna became their first ever £20m ($26m) signing, Carl Rushworth made his loan move permanent for a £22.5m ($30.3m) fee and Caleb Yirenkyi nudged the record up to £23.1m ($31m.)

Three clubs broke their transfer records to sign goalkeepers, with James Trafford costing Leeds £40m ($53.9m) while, like Rushworth, Konstantinos Tsolakis' move to Hull was overtaken by Nobel Mendy's £22m ($29.6m) arrival.

Aston Villa and Ipswich are the other clubs to break their respective records twice while Mamadou Sangare (Brentford), Luka Vuskovic (Brighton) and Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest) were all £40m-plus ($53.9m-plus) club-record buys.

There have been nine moves worth an initial £75m ($101m) or more -- a list completed by City and Arsenal midfielders Ayyoub Bouaddi and Bruno Guimarães -- plus £65m ($87m) moves for Carlos Baleba to Manchester United and Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

On the other side of the balance sheet, Newcastle raised over £235m ($316m) from the three sales of Tonali, Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon while Villa banked £50m-plus ($67m-plus) fees for Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins in addition to Rogers' Chelsea.

stories.headline: Ranking the top 10 NBA rivalries to watch in 2026-27 season
stories.summary: A competitive postseason and buzzy offseason have elevated some of the league's feistiest conflicts.
stories.body:
Some sports rivalries are eternal, due to factors of geography or shared history. Yankees vs. Red Sox. Army vs. Navy. North Carolina vs. Duke.

Yet, others wax and wane in context. For instance, the Chicago Bulls and Detroit Pistons had arguably the NBA's best rivalry during one of the league's best eras; they battled in the playoffs every year from 1988 through 1991, the last three meetings coming in the conference finals.

But Chicago and Detroit have just one playoff matchup in the past 35 years, and they haven't both reached the postseason in the same season since 2008-09. It's difficult for a rivalry to sustain its intensity without regular playoff kindling.

In an ever-changing league, then, it's worth surveying the current rivalry landscape. After a postseason and offseason that elevated some of the feistiest conflicts around, here are the NBA's top 10 rivalries entering the 2026-27 season.

Jump to the top 5

10. Dallas Mavericks vs. Los Angeles Lakers

Our list tips off with one of the strangest NBA rivalries, because many of the first team's fans still adore the second team's best player. But after the Luka Doncic blockbuster in 2025, the Mavericks and Lakers will be inextricably linked for the rest of the 27-year-old future Hall of Famer's career.

Doncic has averaged 37.7 points in three games against the Mavericks since they traded him, and the Lakers are 3-0 in those contests.

Add in the presence of Cooper Flagg, Dallas' new young star, who is now surrounded by so many of Doncic's former running mates (Kyrie Irving, P.J. Washington, Daniel Gafford and so on), and every meeting between these two teams will be a spectacle for the foreseeable future.

9. Cavs owner Dan Gilbert vs. Suns owner Mat Ishbia

The Cleveland Cavaliers' and Phoenix Suns' owners both run Michigan-based mortgage companies, and that business rivalry has carried over to the NBA. The board of governors' vote to allow Ishbia to buy the Suns was unanimous, but with one abstention: Gilbert.

"He doesn't like me and I don't like him," Ishbia said about Gilbert on Bill Simmons' podcast in 2023.

Whether coincidental or not, the Suns and Cavaliers haven't made a trade in the three-plus years since Ishbia bought the former. (The two franchises' last deal, according to Basketball Reference's trade tracker, sent Shaquille O'Neal to Cleveland back in 2009.)

8. Nikola Jokic vs. Victor Wembanyama

From a purely stylistic perspective, this is the best individual rivalry in the NBA right now: the best offensive big man in decades versus a player with a chance to become the best defensive big man ever.

For the most part, Jokic has had Wembanyama's number thus far. He has scored a whopping 37.3 points per game in seven meetings, including at least 40 in each of the past three. But Wembanyama is nine years Jokic's junior, so that balance could start tilting in the other direction soon.

The two All-NBA centers' only showdown last season showed precisely why their individual duels are so thrilling. In an overtime contest in April, Wembanyama tallied 34 points, 18 rebounds, seven assists and five blocks -- only for Jokic to one-up him with 40 points, 13 assists and three blocks, including a majestic Sombor shuffle over his rival to help clinch the win.

7. Boston Celtics vs. Miami Heat

Boston and Miami have the most playoff matchups -- seven -- between any two teams in the 21st century, according to ESPN Research.

Those battles came in two flurries, a decade apart. The Celtics and Heat met in the 2010, 2011 and 2012 postseasons, then took some time off and reengaged their rivalry in the 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024 playoffs. Three of those series went the full seven games, and four came in the conference finals.

Remarkably, the teams' overall record in those seven playoff series is even: 21 wins for Boston, 21 for Miami. And with Giannis Antetokounmpo now a member of the Heat -- after three playoff series of his own as a Milwaukee Buck against Boston -- there is even more star power in this rivalry. It's no wonder that Boston and Miami are slated to play on Christmas afternoon this season.

6. LeBron James vs. Stephen Curry

James and Curry were at the peak of their powers when their rivalry began at the dawn of the Warriors' dynasty in 2015, but the two are no longer quite at that level. James will celebrate his 42nd birthday during this upcoming season, and Curry will turn 39.

Yet a decade after they dueled in four straight Finals, every matchup between the two future Hall of Famers is still must-see TV. They're still talented enough -- both were deserving All-Stars last season -- to entertain, and there's simply so much history infused in all their meetings. Every time James beckons Curry into an isolation, and every time Curry pulls up for a 3-pointer over James' outstretched hand, it brings back the memories of so many high-stakes shots between the two defining players of this era.

Their rivalry gains spiritual bonus points because it has transformed into a friendship over the years, peaking with a gold medal as James and Curry teamed up at the 2024 Olympics.

5. Boston Celtics vs. Los Angeles Lakers

This is the active rivalry that is most rooted in nostalgia. The two winningest NBA franchises have 12 playoff meetings across three eras of basketball history (Russell vs. West, Bird vs. Magic, Pierce vs. Kobe), but just two since the 1980s.

It's difficult, of course, for teams in separate conferences to meet regularly in the playoffs -- especially in the current era of parity, where it's rare for any team to make multiple Finals trips in close succession. Both Boston and Los Angeles look like second-tier contenders entering the 2026-27 season, making it unlikely the two teams will reach the Finals anytime soon and face off for the first time since 2010.

That lack of consistency means Celtics vs. Lakers is no longer the best active rivalry in the NBA. But this rivalry's pageantry and history are so great -- the "Beat L.A." chants so deafening, the broadcast's old highlight reels so inspiring -- that it still warrants a healthy placement on this list.

4. Indiana Pacers vs. New York Knicks

This rivalry started with Reggie Miller on one side and Patrick Ewing and Spike Lee on the other, as the Pacers and Knicks met six times in eight postseasons from 1993 through 2000. That run produced a host of memorable moments, from Miller's choke pantomime and eight points in nine seconds, to Larry Johnson's four-point play.

Then it hibernated for a while; between 2000 and 2024, the two Eastern foes played only once in the postseason, when the Pacers eliminated the best team of the Knicks' Carmelo Anthony era in 2013.

But Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Brunson and their teammates have rekindled an excellent rivalry. The Pacers eliminated the Knicks in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals at Madison Square Garden in 2024, then upset the Knicks again in the conference finals to reach the Finals in 2025 -- a series that featured a momentous comeback and Haliburton's homage to Miller's choke sign.

Both fanbases can point to injuries to downplay the other's accomplishments. A Knicks faithful might say that Indiana only won in 2024 because New York's roster was so injured; Pacers fans might contend that the Knicks' title run was possible because Haliburton's right Achilles tear meant New York didn't have to worry about them in the postseason.

That back-and-forth chatter serves to heighten this rivalry, which should recommence with Haliburton healthy this season and both teams angling to return to the Finals.

3. Denver Nuggets vs. Minnesota Timberwolves

Most of the teams on this list are the NBA's most historically successful franchises -- which makes sense, because more deep playoff runs over decades means more opportunities for high-stakes clashes that stir up bad blood.

That's not the case for Denver and Minnesota, two franchises with a total of one Finals appearance between them. But they've stirred up enough recent drama -- via playoff showdowns in 2023, 2024 and 2026, as well as a 2018 de facto playoff tiebreaker that went to overtime on the last night of the regular season -- to warrant strong placement on this list nonetheless.

This rivalry has just about everything, from immense star power to compelling individual matchups -- most notably Rudy Gobert's efforts to guard Jokic -- to a healthy dislike between locker rooms. "They're all bad defenders," Timberwolves wing Jaden McDaniels taunted during the 2026 playoffs.

The Timberwolves have the upper hand for now: Minnesota eliminated the defending champion Nuggets in 2024 and advanced -- despite multiple injuries -- past their rivals in 2026. But Minnesota made dramatic changes to its roster this offseason, and both teams are now chasing the next two teams on this list rather than each other.

2. Oklahoma City Thunder vs. San Antonio Spurs

These two southwestern giants have met in four playoff series since the Thunder moved from Seattle, and all four were memorably competitive:

In the 2012 conference finals, the Spurs took a 2-0 lead -- as part of a 20-game winning streak -- before the Thunder won four games in a row.
In the 2014 conference finals, the Spurs won Game 6 in overtime to reach the Finals.
In the 2016 second round, the Thunder upset a Spurs team that had won a franchise-record 67 games in the regular season; the Spurs had a 42-1 record at home that season before losing twice against the Thunder in San Antonio.
In the 2026 conference finals, the Spurs eliminated the defending champs in Game 7 in Oklahoma City.

That last series propelled this rivalry to an even greater level, after a regular season in which the Thunder started 24-1 only to drop three games to the Spurs in 13 days. Both teams have electric young backcourts, and Wembanyama and Chet Holmgren have been fierce rivals ever since they dueled on the international youth scene.

This rivalry has a strong case for the No. 1 spot right now, and because both Oklahoma City and San Antonio project to remain among the NBA's title favorites for seasons to come, they're likely to keep adding to that list of memorable playoff series.

Their next battle, though, comes as soon as possible when the Thunder take a trip to San Antonio on opening night.

1. Boston Celtics vs. Philadelphia 76ers

The Celtics and 76ers are the most frequent playoff rivals throughout NBA history. The two franchises have met in 23 playoff series all time, which is well ahead of the second-most-frequent matchup (15 meetings between the Knicks and Celtics).

But in recent seasons the rivalry seemed to be fading because it had grown so one-sided: Until this spring, the 76ers hadn't eliminated Boston since 1982. On the other side of the ledger, the Celtics knocked out Philadelphia in 1985, 2002, 2012, 2018, 2020 and 2023.

That changed this past season, however. First, the 76ers came back from a 3-1 deficit in the first round to stun the Celtics, who were favored not only to beat Philadelphia again, but to return to the Finals. Then, the 76ers traded for longtime Celtic Jaylen Brown, a former Finals MVP for Boston. And finally, they signed James in free agency.

Those transactions in particular add fascinating wrinkles to an already heated rivalry. Presumably, when the two teams meet this season, Brown and Jayson Tatum will spend plenty of time guarding each other as teammates turned rivals. James also folds in his own lengthy individual rivalry with the Celtics, whom he faced in playoff series in 2008, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2017 and 2018; the NBA's all-time scoring leader experienced arguably the best and worst moments of his career against Boston in the playoffs.

At long last, the NBA's most frequent rivalry is once again its fiercest, as well.
